observations: Three photos show a used car engine on a dirt ground, likely in a scrapyard or workshop.
The engine has a black plastic cover with the Volkswagen logo and 'TSI' embossed on it.
The engine appears dirty and used, with visible hoses, belts, and metal components.
Photo 2 shows the front of the engine with the intake manifold, throttle body, and part of the cylinder head.
No visible damage to the engine block or major components, but no proof of functionality or completeness.
The seller claims it is a complete engine, but no accessories like ECU, sensors, or wiring harnesses are shown.

claims.evidence: The engine cover shows 'TSI' and the Volkswagen logo, but no proof of completeness (e.g., ECU, sensors, wiring harness, or accessories) is visible. The photos show the engine body but not the full set of components.

risks.risk: Engine may not be functional or may have internal damage (e.g., blown head gasket, cracked block, worn bearings).
risks.proof: A video showing the engine running or a compression test report.

risks.risk: Missing accessories such as ECU, sensors, wiring harness, or oil filter.
risks.proof: Photos of all included accessories laid out next to the engine.

risks.risk: Engine may have been salvaged from a wrecked or accident-damaged vehicle.
risks.proof: VIN or vehicle history report from the donor car.

proof_requests: Close-up of the engine or gearbox code: the plate, sticker or number stamped on the block or case.
Video of the engine running or a compression test report.
Photos of all included accessories (ECU, sensors, wiring harness, oil filter, etc.).
VIN or vehicle history report from the donor car.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
